items.actClause: AN ACT to amend chapter 915 of the laws of 1982 amending the public authorities law relating to the powers of the state of New York mortgage agency, in relation to the effective date thereof; and to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the powers of the state of New York mortgage agency
items.lawCode: Amd §16, Chap 915 of 1982; amd §2407, Pub Auth L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7582

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend chapter 915 of the laws of 1982 amending the public
authorities law relating to the powers of the state of New York
mortgage agency, in relation to the effective date thereof; and to
amend the public authorities law, in relation to the powers of the
state of New York mortgage agency


 PURPOSE :

This bill would (i) extend the authority of the State of New York
Mortgage Agency ("SONYMA" or "the Agency") to purchase forward
commitment mortgages and to issue new money tax-exempt bonds and new
money taxable bonds, and (ii) increase the maximum amount of SONYMA' s
authority to issue new money tax-exempt bonds.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill would extend SONYMA's authority to purchase
forward commitment mortgages until July 16, 2011.

Section 2 of the bill would (i) extend SONYMA's authority to issue new
money taxable and tax-exempt bonds until July 16, 2011; and (ii)
increase SONYMA's tax-exempt bonding authority by $500 million to a
maximum of $9.22 billion.

Section 3 of the bill provides for an immediate effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :

Under existing law, SONYMA's authority to purchase forward commitment
mortgages and to issue new money taxable bonds is scheduled to sunset
on July 16, 2010. SONYMA is currently authorized to issue up to $8.720
billion of new money tax-exempt bonds and up to $800 million of new
money taxable bonds by July 16, 2010.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

Similar bills have been enacted each year since before 2000 to
increase SONYMA's tax exempt bonding authority and to extend by one
year the sunset dates of SONYMA's authority to purchase forward
commitment mortgages and to issue new money tax-exempt and taxable
bonds.  See Chapter 177 of the Laws of 2009; Chapter 148 of the Laws
of 2008; Chapter 227 of the Laws of 2007; Chapter 138 of the Laws of
2006; Chapter 121 of the Laws of 2005; Chapter 147 of the Laws of
2004; Chapter 141 of the Laws of 2003; Chapter 103 of the Laws of
2002; Chapter 111 of the Laws of 2001; Chapter 132 of the Laws of
2000.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :

SONYMA's statutory authorizations to issue new money tax-exempt bonds
and to purchase forward commitment mortgages are scheduled to sunset
on July 16, 2010. SONYMA's statutory authorization to issue new money
taxable bonds is also scheduled to sunset on July 16, 2010. This bill
would extend the sunset dates for the issuance of new money tax-exempt
bonds and new money taxable bonds, and for the purchase of forward
commitment mortgages until July 16, 2011.

This bill would also increase the maximum amount of new money
tax-exempt bonds which SONYMA is authorized to issue. The increase
being requested is intended to address the borrowing needs of the

Agency in 2010 as a result of a new Federal program and to allow the
Agency to issue bonds for student loan purposes.

The Agency, like most state housing finance agencies throughout the
country, has been adversely impacted in its ability to continue to
offer low interest rate fixed rate mortgage financing to eligible
first-time homebuyers, due to the dramatic events in the financial
markets during late 2008. In order to ameliorate this situation, the
US Department of Treasury recently announced a program that will
permit state housing agencies such as SONYMA to sell tax exempt bonds
to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac (the "GSEs"). The GSEs will securitize
the bonds and simultaneously sell the securities to the Department of
Treasury. The program will enable the Agency to lower its borrowing
costs and as a result, the Agency will be able to once again offer its
mortgages at attractive interest rates. The program runs through the
end of 2010.

In early 2009, the Agency's statute was amended to modernize the
Agency's authority to issue bonds to finance student loans. The Agency
has completed its first bond sale, and expects to make the program a
yearly one. The expectation is that the Agency would issue
approximately $350 million in bonds per year, assuming continuing
demand.

Given the Treasury Department program and the implementation of the
student loan program, the Agency therefore expects a significant
increase in demand. SONYMA's current authority to issue new money
tax-exempt bonds and taxable bonds are insufficient to cover the
current expected demand for mortgages and student loans in the next
few years. This bill would increase SONYMA's authority to issue
additional tax-exempt bonds and notes up to a total maximum amount of
$9.22 billion, which will enable SONYMA to satisfy its expected
mortgage and student loan demand.

 FISCAL IMPACT :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This bill would become effective immediately.

summary: Extends certain provisions relating to the powers of the state of New York mortgage agency.
